searchText: ah. was just going to mention, out of the three you mentioned, I know Etherscan has already implemented 1559 tx stuff for testnets. Sounds like a issue to be solved at the root if you think it's big enough to be a deciding factor in ethereum hfs I think we can all agree more competition for MetaMask and etherscan would be a good things. I suspect those teams would concur 😉 I'm betting on more and more users running local Otterscan installations 🙂 what was the reasoning behind setting all fork blocks to be 3am Europe time? for London <@!552133098075193354> ? Can we try to hit midday UTC for mainnet? seems that 80% of the core devs operate more or less in the UTC timezone with exceptions in West Coast and Australia. So maybe somewhere around 1-3pm UTC would be better? on the other hand lots of infrastructure is in California? where are MetaMask, Infura and Alchemy teams based? <@!489256758989029405> I think the aim was wednesday and the testnet palindrome fork number style forces the hour (which nobody checked) Since on mainnet we generally go with thousands for fork numbers, you have 5 slots per day, so can try to aim for midday On Goerli there is a palindrom every 5000 seconds which is 1.5 hours. As for Ropsten and RInkeby, yes, this is a problem. Ethereum anniversary date doesnt matter but palindrome matters? Why 🙂 because it allows core devs to quickly verify if the fork block looks ok wow <@!488328812501663744> It doesn't. I started it on Rinkeby because why not, then stuck with it because it's fun It's fine to have fun on a testnet Mainnet is production, there the criteria is security, all else secondary https://twitter.com/AndreCronjeTech/status/1412386819635826698?s=20 be careful HF'ing goerli <:pepeGrin:740998005989310464> this has been talked about since the beginning of the year, someone finally did it huh. I imagine this will get dumped pretty quickly.. which is a good thing, testnet coins should be 0 😛 You don't think Goerli would make a good second ETH shard? Eventually there needs to be at least one other shard besides L1 in the beacon chain synchronization - right? Why not Goerli? I would like to hear a compelling argument. It seems to me that it makes perfect sense as (firstly) a L2 scaling solution or (later) as a synchronous ETH shard. The test networks are a place where the core devs can deploy code that may catastrophically fail. Anyone who uses a test network needs to know about and be prepared for this. The entire network could get into a state where it cannot easily recover and all data is lost and that needs to be OK with people. we can discuss this in <#595721451651465227> I didn’t realize there were multiple options for Goerli - will def take it into account for mainnet. <@552133098075193354> so when do you think we can have all data to make a decision regarding the mainnet hf block? I just opened a PR on the eth1.0-specs repo proposing block `12965000`, which would happen between ~13-17h UTC on August 4: https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/223 If no one has any objections, I'll merge it in ~24h and we can go with that. It would be great to have the client releases with the blocks ready for AllCoreDevs this Friday, but even if it's early next week, it should still give us enough time to properly communicate the update. cc: <@&836981603216654336> <@&652918665943056397> <@&595684226221735986> <@&688090867927482525> <@&688101493978562687> I found a EU-friendly block w.r.t. timezone <@!489256758989029405> 🙂 Appreciated, hope it doesn't hit you with the 1pm UTC time. I’m not the one who has to debug a consensus issue if it happens, so I’ll be fine 😄 <@!403707149043105803> got `0xB715077D` for the Fork ID for London with block `12965000` could another team confirm? Thanks! https://github.com/ethereum/eth1.0-specs/pull/223#discussion_r664869718 <@!300026497274478592> got the number, I just propagated it into the spec.
